transcription: Agency-written introduction and background only: the bold summary sentence and the five history paragraphs. The page H1 is supplied as the '# ' title line. Citation line, images and enlarge/download links, the DocsTeach block, the 'Teach with this document.' line, previous/next navigation and the joint-resolution transcript were removed (same treatment as the existing Milestone Documents pages). Em dashes kept as printed. Whitespace normalised.
purpose: library: women's suffrage and the 19th Amendment — a dated chronology from the mid-19th-century movement (lectures, writing, marches, lobbying, civil disobedience) through first introduction in Congress in 1878, nine western states with woman suffrage by 1912, New York in 1917, President Wilson's 1918 shift, House passage May 21, 1919 and the Senate two weeks later, Tennessee as the 36th ratifying state on August 18, 1920, to Secretary of State Bainbridge Colby's certification on August 26, 1920 — plus the limits of ratification (discriminatory state laws kept many minority women unable to vote into the 20th century). Fits timeline ordering and quiz cards with predict-then-reveal on the dates and the three-fourths threshold.
